## Brand Positioning

# BKT Advisory — Brand Positioning

> Canonical brand spec for John Burkhardt / BKT Advisory across the portfolio,
> estimator, and every Claude surface. `portable` — vendored to spokes and the
> Web/Designer bundle. Decisions locked with John, 2026-06-24.

## Positioning statement
**John Burkhardt is the bridge between the Salesforce ecosystem and enterprise AI** —
turning platform and AI complexity into a predictable growth engine for revenue teams.

## Identity
- **Eyebrow / title:** `Salesforce + Enterprise AI Architect`
- **Role line:** `Founder & Principal Consultant`
- **Hero headline (chosen):** *Where the Salesforce ecosystem meets enterprise AI.*
- **Hero headline (alt, clarity-forward):** *Turn Salesforce and AI complexity into a predictable growth engine.*

## Four pillars
1. **Intersection** — Salesforce depth × enterprise-AI fluency; few operate credibly in both.
2. **Complexity → Clarity** — translate platform/AI sprawl into a clear, staged plan.
3. **Executive goals → Technical delivery** — own the path from boardroom outcome to shipped system.
4. **Predictable, compounding revenue** — RevOps that builds durable pipeline, not one-off wins.

## Lexicon
- **System of record** = Salesforce. **System of action** = AI agents. **System of growth** = RevOps.
- Voice: senior, precise, outcome-first, calm. Speak to revenue/operations leaders.
- **Banned words:** operationalize, leverage (verb), seamless, synergize, cutting-edge, supercharge.

## Proof points (single source of truth — converge all surfaces)
- **8x Salesforce Certified** (the canonical cert count — was inconsistent 5x/7x/8x across files).
- **$837M+ Transactions Closed** · **2x Qualified Pipeline** · **Weeks → Days** delivery.

## Usage
- Marketing surfaces (Hero, Services, About, Process, CTAs) lead with **outcomes**, then capability.
- Keep one eyebrow and one cert number across **both** repos (portfolio + estimator).
- This doc is the spec; copy is reviewed against it. UI/visual rules live in each repo's
  `docs/conventions/design-system.md`.

## Auto-Submission Rules (ADR-006)

| ID | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BR-130 | Submission autonomy follows `user_settings.review_mode`: `review` = explicit JB approval per application; `assist` = scores ≥ threshold auto-queue as approved; `auto` = scores ≥ threshold submit autonomously within guardrails | ADR-006 |
| BR-131 | All autonomy guardrails (score threshold, credits/budget, daily cap, pause) are enforced server-side in the submission worker from `user_settings`; client state is never trusted for submission decisions. **Authorization to submit is derived server-side from `user_settings.review_mode` plus the server-side `match_score`/threshold, OR from an explicit `approval` `application_events` row — never from the client-supplied `application_queue.queued_by` (audit-only).** A claimed row lacking both stays `approved` (`awaiting_approval`) and is never cancelled for lacking authorization | ADR-006 |
| BR-132 | `user_settings.paused = true` is an immediate kill switch: the worker submits nothing for that user while set | ADR-006 |
| BR-133 | Submission workflow state lives in `application_queue` (one row per application, `UNIQUE (application_id)`); every attempt and outcome also writes an `application_events` row — the event log remains the source of truth | ADR-006, BR-004 |
| BR-134 | Submission is API-first (`application_method` `api`/`ats` → ATS endpoint adapters); browser-channel postings submit via Browserbase + Stagehand. BR-032/033/034 remain binding — postings that cannot be submitted within those rules fail to manual with a recorded reason | ADR-006, BR-032, BR-033, BR-034 |
| BR-135 | An application transitions `discovery → applied` only on confirmed successful submission (or explicit JB manual action); queueing alone never changes stage | ADR-006, BR-004 |
| BR-136 | Each submission decrements `user_settings.credits` atomically; zero credits or exhausted monthly budget halts assist/auto queueing and submission until replenished | ADR-006 |
| BR-146 | The submission worker defaults to a zero-side-effect dry-run; real submissions fire only when `SUBMISSION_LIVE=true` AND the resolved channel's config is present. Absent config (no ATS board/payload, no Browserbase key) fails to manual with a recorded reason — the worker never blind-fires (BR-032/033/034 remain binding) | ADR-006, BR-134 |
| BR-147 | A submission credit is charged atomically at claim (`claim_submission`) and refunded on failure or stuck-expiry (`finalize_submission`/`expire_stuck_submitting`), so only a confirmed successful submission ultimately consumes a credit. **A row stuck in `submitting` past the cutoff is moved to TERMINAL `failed` (not back to `approved`) — it may have submitted externally, so it is never auto-resubmitted and requires manual reconciliation; the expiry writes a `submission_attempt` event with `outcome='unconfirmed'` and refunds the correct per-user credit count** | ADR-006, BR-136 |
| BR-148 | Clients may only create the user-owned queue statuses (`pending_approval`/`approved`) or move a row to `cancelled`; `submitting`/`submitted`/`failed` are written exclusively by the service-role worker, which re-validates every guardrail server-side regardless of the client-supplied `status`/`queued_by`. **The worker additionally enforces application ownership (the queued `application_id` must belong to the queue row's `user_id`) at claim time (returns `not_owned`), and RLS defense-in-depth requires the inserted `application_id` to belong to `auth.uid()`** | ADR-006, BR-131, BR-133, BR-005 |

| ID | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BR-140 | Real match scoring runs through the thin `score-job-fit` Edge Function (routed `match_scoring` → Claude Opus 4.6 / anthropic). The function performs no DB writes and uses no service-role key; cost-gating, `ai_scores` persistence, and `ai_model_usage` logging stay client-side in `aiScoringService` | ADR-007, BR-103, BR-122 |
| BR-141 | When `match_scoring` is blocked by the cost cap (BR-052) or the `score-job-fit` call errors, the deterministic heuristic (`pipelineService.scoreJobFit`) is persisted as the fallback, flagged in `ai_scores.reasoning_trace` with `source = 'heuristic_fallback'` and a `reason` (`cost_cap` / `edge_function_error`), so the dashboard always receives a score | ADR-007, BR-052, BR-024 |
| BR-142 | The persisted recommendation is always derived from `overall_score` via the BR-020/021/022 thresholds (`getScoreLabel` / `toDbRecommendation`); the LLM's own recommendation is advisory only and is never persisted as-is — no threshold literals live outside `aiScoringService` | ADR-007, BR-020, BR-021, BR-022, AI-RULE-001 |
| BR-143 | Document generation runs through the thin `generate-document` Edge Function (routed `cover_letter_generation` → anthropic Opus, `resume_rewriting` → openai GPT-5). The function performs no DB writes and uses no service-role key; cost-gating, persistence, and usage logging stay client-side in `documentGenerationService`. On any Edge error the deterministic template builder is the fallback, flagged `metadata.source = 'template_fallback'` | ADR-008, BR-122, BR-052 |
| BR-144 | Generated documents are persisted to the `documents` table only when persistence is explicitly requested (the DocBuilder align path), reusing `documentStorageService.createDocumentVersion` (Storage + versioned row, content_hash, RLS, BR-070/071); the submission-packet flow persists and links separately, so generation never double-writes | ADR-008, BR-070, BR-071, BR-007 |
| BR-145 | The auto-apply dashboard "Applications Submitted" stat is derived from `applications` DB truth — an application counts as submitted when `submitted_at` is set or its stage is a post-`discovery` happy-path stage (applied … hired) — never from client/localStorage state; demo mode shows a stable seed figure | BR-135, BR-013 |

## Manual Apply & Apply-Macro Rules (ADR-009)

| ID | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BR-149 | In `review`/`assist` (Hybrid) modes, the Dashboard green "Apply" and the dashboard JD-sidebar Apply buttons open the job's `source_url` in a new tab and move the application to a view-model **Manual / In-progress** status. The application's `stage` stays `discovery`; the in-progress marker is a client-written `application_events` row (`event_type='submission_attempt'`, `actor='jb_manual'`, `metadata.outcome='in_progress'`, `metadata.source='manual-apply'`). A follow-up **"Mark as applied"** action fires the audited `discovery → applied` transition via the `transition_stage` RPC. No new pipeline stage is introduced (BR-002/BR-013 unaffected); in `auto` mode the button keeps its existing auto-apply behavior | ADR-009, BR-002, BR-130, BR-135 |
| BR-150 | Match-scoring **input** prefers the user's uploaded master-resume text (read from the `documents` bucket when a `.txt` resume exists, via `fetchCandidateResumeText`) over the hardcoded `masterProfile` keyword set; when no extractable text exists it falls back to the keyword profile (no client-side PDF parsing). Resume text is length-capped (≈12k chars) to bound `tokens_in`; the `$75/user/month` cost cap (BR-052) and the heuristic fallback (BR-141) are unchanged. Populating a pre-extracted `master_resume_text` via real PDF extraction is a documented follow-up | ADR-009, ADR-007, BR-140, BR-141 |
| BR-151 | The Apply-Macro browser extension is **human-in-the-loop only**: it autofills ATS form fields from the user's own (RLS-scoped) profile/resume but **never auto-submits** (`submit.autoClick = false`), never bypasses CAPTCHAs, auth walls, or rate limits, and embeds **no** LLM or service-role key — match scoring is brokered through the JWT-gated `score-job-fit` Edge Function (keys stay Supabase secrets). Anything the macro cannot complete is left for the human. This complements, and does not reverse, ADR-006's deferral of autonomous browser submission | ADR-009, BR-032, BR-033, BR-034, BR-122 |
| BR-152 | The user's candidate profile (identity + eligibility PII) is **self-served** from Preferences → "Job Preferences" and persisted to `candidate_profiles` via `candidateProfileWriteService.upsertCandidateProfile` (one row per user, `onConflict: 'user_id'`, `user_id` forced from the trusted session — never from input). This is the single source of the PII that apply-macro autofill and server-side submission (`_shared/submission/candidate.ts`) read; manual SQL seeding is no longer required | ADR-012, BR-004, BR-005, BR-122 |
| BR-153 | Application answers use **hybrid storage**: fixed EEO / voluntary-disclosure answers live in `candidate_profiles.eeo_disclosures` jsonb (`gender, race_ethnicity, hispanic_latino, veteran_status, disability_status`); arbitrary / reusable custom screener Q&A live in the `application_answers` table (UNIQUE `(user_id, question_key)`, own-row RLS). Both are editable from the Preferences "Answer Library" tab | ADR-012, BR-005 |
| BR-154 | Apply-macro choice / `react-select` autofill is **anti-collision**: an option is matched by exact label first, then a unique prefix, then a unique substring — an ambiguous or absent match is **reported, never guessed** (e.g. `"Male"` must not select the `"Female"` that contains it). This is what makes EEO / eligibility dropdowns safe to autofill (UAT-4, §5.2 — never fill the wrong field) | ADR-012, BR-151 |
| BR-155 | EEO / demographic disclosures and custom screener answers are **autofill-only** and are **never** included in the `score-job-fit` scoring `profile` — only fit-relevant fields (location, work authorization, master-resume text) reach the LLM. No contact PII, EEO, or answers are sent to any model provider | ADR-011, ADR-012, BR-122 |

## Headless Prep & Prepared Applications Rules (ADR-013)

| Rule | Statement | Refs |
| ---- | --------- | ---- |
| BR-156 | A prepared field flagged `is_sensitive = true` (EEO/demographic, work authorization, salary/compensation, security clearance, legal attestation) is **always review-gated and never auto-filled**. Enforced in the database: a `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` trigger (`fn_prepared_field_force_gate`) forces `review_gate = true` whenever `is_sensitive = true`, and `CHECK (NOT is_sensitive OR review_gate)` guarantees it. The server mapper (`fieldMap`) and the extension's `preparedFill` redundantly exclude sensitive fields — three independent layers | ADR-013, BR-151 |
| BR-157 | Auto-mode unattended prep gates on the adapter's **`antibot_tier`**, never a hard-coded platform name. Allowed only when ALL hold: family in the low tier {greenhouse, lever, ashby, smartrecruiters}; no sensitive/legal field in the schema; `match_score ≥ 75`; source is a read-API surface. Any failure → `status='needs_review'` with a `gating_reason`. Workday/LinkedIn/Indeed are never Auto-eligible and are never headless-read (`buildReadEndpoint` returns null → `needs_review`/`blocked`) | ADR-013 |
| BR-158 | Prep is **not event-sourced** into `application_events`: it changes no `applications.stage` and may precede any `applications` row. `prepared_applications` is self-auditing (`status` + `gating_reason` + timestamps); the `discovery → applied` event is written by the existing submit flow when the human submits | ADR-013, BR-002 |
| BR-159 | The on-demand `prepare-application` Edge Function is **RLS-scoped to the caller** — built with the public anon key + the caller's forwarded JWT, `user_id` derived from `auth.getUser()` (never the request body), and **no service-role key** on the on-demand path (the cron branch is a guarded scaffold returning 403/501). It **reads** an ATS schema (auth-free public GET) and **never submits** | ADR-013, BR-004, BR-005, BR-122, BR-151 |
| BR-160 | The server `field_key` vocabulary is **identical** to the extension payload keys (`first_name … eeo_*`, custom screeners as `answer:<question_key>`), so the extension consumes server-prepared fields verbatim. AI free-text drafts (`free_text_draft`, Phase 5 scaffold) are **always** review-gated and never auto-submitted; EEO/answers are never sent to the LLM | ADR-013, ADR-011, BR-155 |
| BR-161 | Resume / cover-letter builder uploads are parsed **client-side at zero API cost** by `resumeFileExtractor.extractResumeText`: PDF via `pdfjs-dist`, DOCX via `fflate` (unzip `word/document.xml`), TXT/MD via `File.text()`. Both heavy libraries are dynamically imported (code-split, on-demand) and pdf.js is never imported at module top level. Extracted text is transcribed **verbatim** into the builder via `transcribeResume` (not rewritten — contrast Auto-Align/ADR-008). On extraction failure (scanned/image PDF, legacy `.doc`, unreadable file) the user is shown the paste-text fallback with the extractor's error. The history row records the **real** `file.size`. This serves the builder upload path only; the match-scoring input path (BR-150) is unchanged | ADR-017, BR-074, BR-150 |
| BR-162 | Uploading a resume **stores the file + its extracted text only** (`DocItem.rawText`); it never auto-parses or auto-opens the builder. Transcription into structured sections happens **lazily, on demand**, when the user opens the Resume Builder for that item (`openInBuilder` → `transcribeResume`). `transcribeResume` handles two input regimes — Markdown (`##`/`**`/`-`/`[label](url)`) and extracted prose (ALL-CAPS or tab-indented PDF/DOCX) — with broadened section matchers ("Executive Summary", "Professional Work Experience", "Core Competencies"/"Areas of Expertise", "Education & Certifications") and preserves structure: grouped skill categories stay one chip each (no comma over-split), each employer keeps its own role/dates/bullets, degrees merge with their institution, and certifications parse into a **dedicated `ResumeContent.certifications` field** (cert lines are split out even from a combined "Education & Certifications" section) rendered as its own Certifications section in the builder + paper. Builder `ResumeContent` is **UI-only**; this does not touch the Review/Hybrid/Auto-Mode apply pipeline, which reads `candidate_profiles`/`documents` | ADR-017, BR-074, BR-161 |
| BR-163 | Uploading a resume (authenticated) persists its **client-extracted text** as a new plain-text `documents` resume version via `saveUploadedResumeText` → `createDocumentVersion`, so job match-scoring (`fetchCandidateResumeText` → `buildScoringProfile` → `score-job-fit`) uses the candidate's real PDF/DOCX resume instead of the keyword fallback — closing the BR-150 follow-up. Best-effort + non-blocking: on any failure scoring falls back exactly as before (BR-150). The ~12k-char scoring cap (BR-150), the `$75/mo` cost cap (BR-050/052), and the heuristic fallback (BR-141) are unchanged; demo mode (no `userId`) skips persistence | BR-150, ADR-009, BR-161 |
| BR-164 | The Documents screen (resumes + cover letters) shows **only the user's real, RLS-scoped `documents`** — never demo/seed data. The history loads from `listDocuments(userId, type)`; the **Preview shows the true stored document text verbatim** (no parsing/restyling); structured parsing into the builder happens **only on open** (`transcribeResume`/`transcribeLetter`). Builder edits **save durably** to the `documents` table: a debounced (~1.2 s) autosave serializes the structured content back to round-trippable Markdown (`serializeResume`/`serializeLetter`) and writes it — `createDocumentVersion` on first save, then `updateDocumentContent` **in place** (one editing session = one version, no per-keystroke spam) — driving a real Saving/Saved indicator from the actual DB write (the fake timer is removed). Persisted resume text doubles as the scoring source (BR-163). Delete removes the storage object + row. Stored as text (no schema migration); custom formatting may shift slightly on the text round-trip. Builder `ResumeContent`/`LetterContent` stay UI-only (no apply-pipeline impact) | ADR-017, BR-074, BR-161, BR-163 |
| BR-165 | Document uploads store the **ACTUAL file**, not just text: `uploadDocumentFile` writes the original binary to the `documents` bucket (`original_path`) **and** the extracted text as a `.txt` (`storage_path`, the scoring source) in one `documents` row carrying `file_name`/`mime_type`. The library (`listDocuments`) lists rows by **real filename** and **excludes `is_locked` rows** (submission artifacts linked to applications via `application_materials` — never shown/edited in the library). Preview renders the real document: **PDF via a signed-URL `<iframe>`**, DOCX as extracted text + **Download original**, MD/TXT as text. `deleteDocument` removes **both** storage objects + the row. The broken trash was caused by **missing DELETE RLS policies** on `public.documents` and the `documents` storage bucket — added in migration `20260626000001` (the additive `file_name`/`mime_type`/`original_path`/`builder_config` columns + both DELETE policies). `builder_config` is reserved for Phase 2 (per-section bullet toggles + custom-sections engine). Direct SQL deletes on `storage.objects` are blocked by Supabase — deletes go through the Storage API | ADR-017, BR-150, BR-163, BR-164 |
| BR-166 | The resume builder exposes **per-section bullet toggles** (Experience / Skills / Education / Certifications) and **up to 4 custom sections** with a format each (`bullets` / `table` / `text`), persisted **per resume** in `documents.builder_config` (jsonb). `defaultBuilderConfig()` matches the prior rendering (experience + certifications already bulleted) so a resume looks unchanged until the user toggles. `DocPaper` renders each section per its toggle and renders custom sections by format (bullets = list, table = one row per line with `|`-split cells, text = paragraph block). Config is coerced defensively from the untyped jsonb via `parseBuilderConfig` and saved by the builder's debounced autosave — `createDocumentVersion`/`updateDocumentContent` accept an optional `builderConfig`, and the autosave signature includes the config so toggle/custom-section edits trigger a save. **Builder-only**: the `.txt` scoring source is the serialized standard sections; custom-section content lives only in `builder_config` (no apply-pipeline/scoring impact) | BR-164, BR-165 |
| BR-167 | **Builder autosave requires a storage UPDATE policy.** In-place saves overwrite the `.txt` via storage `upsert` (= UPDATE on `storage.objects`); the documents bucket had INSERT/SELECT/DELETE but no UPDATE policy, so every edit to an already-saved/uploaded resume was RLS-denied (HTTP 400 "new row violates row-level security policy") and **silently failed to persist** — fixed by migration `20260626000002` (`"Documents bucket: update own files"`, same uid-folder clause). Resume content sections are **drag-to-reorder**: `builder_config.sectionOrder` holds the order of the standard keys interleaved with custom-section ids (Summary is always first and not included); `effectiveSectionOrder` normalizes it (drops stale, appends missing) so it is always complete. The builder renders each content section editor in that order with a grip handle (native HTML5 drag-and-drop) and `DocPaper` renders the paper in the same order. Experience bullets are sanitized to one continuous sentence each (hard line breaks collapsed to spaces, like the summary) | BR-164, BR-166 |

## Patterns

# PAT-001 — Four-state component contract

## Problem
Components that fetch or depend on async data routinely ship only the happy
("success") path. Loading flicker, blank screens on empty data, and silent
failures are the most common UX defects across all BKT surfaces.

## Pattern
Every data-bound component must explicitly handle **all four** states —
`loading`, `empty`, `error`, `success` — before it is considered done. This is a
review gate (the `emil-design-eng` / `ui-ux` agents enforce it) and applies in
every BKT repo, so it is `portable`.

## Example
```tsx
function JobList({ query }: { query: UseQueryResult<Job[]> }) {
  if (query.isLoading) return <ListSkeleton rows={5} />        // loading
  if (query.isError)   return <ErrorState onRetry={query.refetch} /> // error
  if (!query.data?.length) return <EmptyState label="No jobs yet" /> // empty
  return <ul>{query.data.map((j) => <JobRow key={j.id} job={j} />)}</ul> // success
}
```

## When not to use
Purely presentational components with no async/empty dimension (e.g. a static
`Badge`) only need `success`. Don't manufacture states that can't occur.

---

# PAT-002 — Hash-verified flat-copy vendoring

## Problem
Sharing assets (skills, agents, knowledge) across independently-deployed repos
can't rely on symlinks or a package registry: each repo is its own git root on
Vercel/Replit, and symlinks break in those checkouts. But blind copies silently
rot — a spoke's copy drifts from the hub and nobody notices.

## Pattern
Copy assets as **flat files**, and record a `sha256` per file in the spoke's
`skills-lock.json` (`sourceType: "local"`, hub SHA). A `--check` mode recomputes
hashes and fails on any mismatch (a hand-edited vendored file) or missing file.
Editing happens **only in the hub**; spokes re-sync. This is `hub-only` because
it documents this repo's own porting machinery (`scripts/sync-claude-kit.mjs`).

## Example
```bash
# vendor + record hashes
node scripts/sync-claude-kit.mjs --target ../bktAdvisory --profile full
# later, in CI or a spoke PR — fails (exit 1) if any vendored file drifted
node scripts/sync-claude-kit.mjs --target ../bktAdvisory --check
```

## When not to use
When both ends share one deploy/git root (a true monorepo), prefer a workspace
package or symlink — the hash dance is overhead you don't need.
